title: Campaign workspace and Roster
question: Choose the layout for finding participants and keeping their campaign context close at hand. All three retain the existing discovery and note/tag capabilities.

options.label: Search-first roster
options.thesis: A broad search field leads into a full-width roster; participant details open over the field.
options.viewport: Campaign identity and Route Markers sit above search, a collapsible filter shelf, and a broad roster.
options.risk: The drawer temporarily covers part of the roster while a participant is open.

options.label: Roster beside context
options.thesis: Keep the roster and the selected participant visible side by side during desktop work.
options.viewport: Shared identity and route lead into a broad roster and a narrower participant panel; mobile uses a full-screen detail sheet.
options.risk: Side-by-side context gives the roster less horizontal room for placement evidence.

options.label: Roster above workbench
options.thesis: A full-width roster stays above a horizontal participant workbench with identity, placement evidence, and observations.
options.viewport: Identity, route, and discovery lead to roster rows; selecting a row reveals a divided workbench immediately below the bounded roster.
options.risk: The workbench reduces the number of roster rows visible at once on shorter screens.
